Subject: Load plan + ask: temporary credits for POC 99th/95th validation

Hi Irene / Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team loved the predictability of the routing and the dashboard traces. We're ready to run a short overnight soak to validate 95th/99th latency stability under a production-like mix.

Quick ask: can Redwood provision a temporary credit bridge so we can run a 12-hour concentrated load (mostly small chat requests with occasional long generations) on our dedicated POC fleet? We prepared a traffic plan attached (bytecart_traffic_plan_v2.xlsx) and a sample request distribution (poc-mat-june-traffic.json). Target: 10k RPS burst windows with sustained 2k RPS baseline, validating p95 and p99 across endpoints.

Requirements/constraints:
- Start window: 10/08 22:00 PT -> 10/09 10:00 PT (12 hours)
- Need an additional 120k token-equivalent credits to avoid throttling during peak ramps
- We will provide a signed PO if you need procurement records, but would prefer a provisional top-up to avoid waiting on finance.

Can you confirm what you can provision and whether any routing policy adjustments are advisable for stability?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Doe
Head of DataOps, ByteCart

Alex — appreciated the details and the clean traffic plan. Short answer: yes, we can provide a provisional credit bridge for the overnight soak.

Proposed approach:
- Interim top-up: 130,000 token-equivalent provisional credits to be applied to your POC sandbox account, active 10/08 21:30 PT to 10/09 11:00 PT (buffers for pre/post ramps).
- Ops guardrails: We'll put a soft throttle at 12k RPS and enable aggressive KV prefix caching for your baseline flows to preserve p95.
- Post-run deliverables: we'll share per-token cost and a per-route latency breakdown within 48 hours.

If that works, I will route a formal approval to Billing for a one-time promotional credit grant pending your PO. Jonas / Ben — can you review for any budget or SLA caveats?

Irene Choi
